correctness.rationale: The affine simplex mass matrix is proportional to G=I+11^T on the n=d+1 nodes and has metric ratio κ=n+1. A nodal input/output difference pair (u,v) of the convex projection satisfies ||v||²≤<u,v>, so vv^T/<u,v> (or zero) is a positive contraction taking u to v. Orthogonal projections have G-norm at most (κ+1)/(2√κ) by the Wielandt angle estimate; the spectral-layer integral transfers this to contractions and the sum of element norms gives the mesh estimate. For exact attainment, the stated identity/zero blocks (even n) or the three rank-one directions plus cancelling blocks (odd n) give sum D_i h=nh/2. For the normalized constant mode e, z=2De−e is a unit mean-zero mode; δ=e/κ+z gives Dδ=(1+1/κ)(e+z)/2 and ratio (κ+1)/(2√κ). The rank-one perturbations commute with their nodal bases, so a sufficiently small finite perturbation realizes these actions by actual clipping, including after fixed-coordinate embedding for m>2. For the scalar selector with 1≤k≤n active nodes, eliminating inactive inputs by a Schur complement gives denominator metric I+11^T/(n−k+1) on the active coordinates and numerator metric I+11^T; the constant active direction gives squared factor (k+1)(n−k+1)/(n+1). The empty selector has norm zero, not one as the unqualified selector expression in the proof would suggest; it is immaterial to the maximum, attained by the balanced nonempty selector and realizable by finite scalar clipping differences. Positive lumped weights preserve nodewise nonexpansivity, with equality on interval-interior fields. All sharpness claims are universal over meshes, not assertions of sharpness on every mesh. These are analytic checks of the arbitrary-dimension proof and exact witnesses; the supplied diagnostic code was inspected, not executed.
